method.label: Reduce cubes and use a power cycle

annotationRationale: The solution combines congruences term by term and evaluates a large power through its residue cycle. Factorization supplies the divisibility proof for the cube congruence.
sourceMethod: Follows the official factorization of n cubed minus n, reduction of the sum modulo 6, and alternating power remainders.

review.mathCheck: The product (n−1)n(n+1) is divisible by both 2 and 3, so n³≡n modulo 6. Consequently the cube sum is congruent to 2^2018, whose alternating residues 2,4 give remainder 4. Answer E is correct; strict increase is unnecessary for this deduction.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, reworded adaptation of official Solution 16, page 7: factor n³−n, sum the congruences, then use the even position in the power cycle.
review.annotationCheck: The congruence and power-cycle reasoning is fully explained. Factorization is correctly distinguished as supporting knowledge.
